evidence:
Independent exact-proposal review: I read only the new repair packet and its official primary source, https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07006v1#S3. I did not read the semantic registry, earlier fidelity verdicts, source reviews or repair decisions. I am neither andi-gd-worker nor gd_blind and did not author this proposal. This decision concerns proposal ASTIS-REPAIR-ANDI-GD-NONNEGATIVE-STEP only; compilation was not repeated or used to establish necessity.

Primary-source check: Section 3 explicitly assumes C² smoothness. Theorem 3.3 prints only h≤1/β. Definition 3.2 places its condition-number discussion in κ=β/α≥1. The proposed overlay preserves these source conventions, adding just h≥0. This is a correction of the literal all-real-step reading; an intended convention that a step size is nonnegative would instead make it an explicit statement of that convention.

Counterexample independently verified: let f(t)=t²/2 on ℝ, α=β=1. Its gradient is t and Hessian is 1, so it is C², 1-strongly convex and 1-smooth, with strictly positive reciprocal and condition-number domains. For x=0,y=1, T(y)−T(x)=1−h. At h=−1 the printed upper-step bound is satisfied, while the proposed conclusion reads 2≤√2 and is false; the square-root argument is 2>0, so this counterexample uses the ordinary real square root with no totalization issue. More generally for any h<0, put a=1−h>1. Then |1−h|=a, the claimed factor is √a, and a²−a=h(h−1)>0. Thus every negative step fails on this single admissible objective.

Mathematical sufficiency checked independently: write v=y−x, d=∇f(y)−∇f(x), p=⟨d,v⟩. The source convexity/smoothness hypotheses give p≥α‖v‖²≥0 and ‖d‖²≤βp. With 0≤h≤1/β and β>0, h²‖d‖²≤h²βp≤hp. Consequently ‖v−hd‖²=‖v‖²−2hp+h²‖d‖²≤‖v‖²−hp≤(1−αh)‖v‖². These two multiplications require h≥0; they are not mere compiler conveniences. Taking ordinary square roots gives the unchanged claimed factor on the source square-root domain.

Positive reciprocal and square-root domains: this repair retains β>0 for 1/β. In the positive condition-number setting, α>0 and κ=β/α≥1 give α≤β, so 0≤αh≤α/β≤1 and 1−αh≥0. If the single-step theorem includes α=0, its factor is 1 and the same β>0 requirement remains; no κ is needed for that nonexpansive case. Equivalently in nontrivial Euclidean space, the C² curvature lower and smoothness upper bounds imply α≤β by evaluating a nonzero direction. The repaired claim is not interpreted as a new zero-denominator or negative-square-root convention, nor as an extension to degenerate singleton spaces with incompatible moduli. Such extensions belong to the local Lean theorem, not this source repair.

Minimality: h=0 yields T=identity and √(1−αh)=1, hence equality, so imposing h>0 would unnecessarily discard a valid endpoint. The upper endpoint h=1/β is retained, including α=β when the factor is zero. Every negative h must be excluded for a guarantee uniform over the stated source class, as the quadratic above shows. Thus among modifications of the printed step interval leaving the objective class and conclusion fixed, adding h≥0 is the minimal necessary exclusion. This does not assert that every individual objective fails at every negative step: constant objectives can be exceptions, which do not rescue the universal source theorem.

Scope separation: the candidate Lean statement is on complete real inner-product spaces with C¹ regularity, a quadratic upper model, nonnegative α,β, the division-free βh≤1, and total Real.sqrt. Those are distinct generalizations/formal conventions and are not accepted here as source repairs. The exact proposal retains C² Euclidean space, the reciprocal step bound and ordinary square-root domains. It does not claim admission of the iterated-distance theorem, logarithmic complexity result, the full candidate publication context, or any separate typographical correction in a proof display. Keeping the pinned source statement unchanged with a separately accepted overlay is appropriate.

Decision: accept this exact assumption-addition proposal as mathematically necessary for the literal all-real-step formulation and sufficient on the preserved source domain. No modification to this proposal is required; no additional smoothness, dimension assumption, strict step positivity or changed conclusion is justified by the repair.
